title: Dispatch: PR #546 repair - capability report membership and ledger invariants (F5,F7)
description:
PR #546 review repair, capability half. Findings F5 and F7 of the 2026-09-13
review by jbongaarts on head e73b588. Read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4` and the
note beginning "=== PR #546 REVIEW" IN FULL before writing code: it carries the
supervisor's verification of each finding and design decision D2, which is
already made and is NOT yours to revisit.

Authority: ADR 0020 §3; docs/design/evidence-trust-model.md; the CLOSED W13 bead
eshyra-olc5.6 (owns capability CONTRACT SHAPE) and eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 (owns
selected-capability MEMBERSHIP - this bead owns neither).

DO NOT TOUCH the relationship half: recordRelationships.ts,
recordRelationshipDeclarations.ts, record-relationships.json, expansion.ts,
harness.ts, traceProjection.ts, packLoader.ts, test/rules/. A sibling child owns
those.

=== F5 (MATERIAL) The move silently changed the audit bundle's reported membership ===
Before this PR the audit bundle's `RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS` held
THREE rule contracts. The shared runtime map now also holds
`derived-magic-item-clauses-v1` (deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts:82), and
`buildRuleDispositionReport` still emits
`Object.values(RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS)`
(ruleDispositions.ts:3612), so the generated report went from three contract
identities to FOUR. The corroborating symptom is the special case at
ruleDispositions.ts:3042, where `validateRuleDeterministicCapabilityContracts`
has to exempt `derived-magic-item-clauses-v1` because it is not a registered
tool - the adapter is reporting a different CLASS of contract than it was
reviewed for.

This is a membership change made inside a mechanism-only bead. W13 does establish
the magic-item readiness contract as real; the defect is not its existence, it is
that this PR decided a capability REPORT's membership, which belongs to
eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.

DESIGN DECISION D2, ALREADY MADE - implement exactly this: PRESERVE THE AUDIT
REPORT'S PRIOR REVIEWED MEMBERSHIP. The rule-disposition report emits the three
rule contracts it has always emitted. The magic-item readiness contract stays a
real member of the RUNTIME ledger (packet presentation and lookup are unchanged)
but is outside that report's reviewed scope. Because the report no longer carries
a non-tool contract, the `derived-magic-item-clauses-v1` exemption at :3042 goes
away with it - if you find yourself keeping that exemption, the split is wrong.
Do not instead delete the contract from the ledger, and do not ask the report to
grow a fourth member.

Shape it so the runtime ledger and the report share ONE definition of every row
they both use - re-introducing a second copy is the defect the previous round
fixed (see the bead's ROUND 1 review note, finding X1).

R7 MUST BE RE-GROUNDED. The current R7 test pins a newly authored four-row set, so
it cannot detect the very drift it is supposed to catch - a pin authored AFTER a
change ratifies it. Compare against the PRE-MOVE identities as they exist on
`origin/main` (read
`git show origin/main:packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts`
and take the three contract revisions, eight bindings and thirty-one disposition
keys from there), and assert the post-move REPORT still emits exactly those. A
`toBe` identity check that each shared name resolves to the single runtime
definition is still wanted, but it is not the membership proof.

Evidence: a test that fails if the report's contract identities, binding pairs, or
disposition keys differ from the pre-move set; and a test that the runtime ledger
still knows the magic-item revision even though the report does not list it.

=== F7 The exported constructor does not enforce identity/uniqueness ===
`createDeterministicCapabilityLedger` rejects an unknown contract key and a key
that is both bound and dispositioned, and nothing else. It accepts:
  * duplicate identical `(ruleKey, capability)` bindings -> duplicate packet
    capability entries for one candidate;
  * a registry key whose `contract.revision` names a DIFFERENT identity -> the
    binding selects one lookup key while the packet advertises another revision;
  * a disposition map key whose `disposition.ruleKey` names another record ->
    lookup returns a disposition identifying a different rule.
The global `DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_LEDGER` is built through this weaker path.
The audit-bundle validator is a separate caller and is NOT the constructor's
guarantee - a runtime consumer must not depend on an audit-only path happening
to run.

REQUIRED: the exported constructor establishes every identity and uniqueness
invariant its callers rely on, failing closed BEFORE any lookup or packet
presentation. Constructor tests for duplicate `(ruleKey, capability)`,
registry-key vs `contract.revision` mismatch, and disposition-key vs
`disposition.ruleKey` mismatch. Keep the existing unknown-contract and
overlap cases passing.

=== VERIFICATION ===
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Run the
audit-bundle script and report whether the generated report changed; the intended
outcome is that its contract membership returns to the pre-move three. Explain any
other diff.

=== PROHIBITIONS ===
Assert identities, never counts. No corpus-wide capability inventory or
completeness claim. No change to the W13 contract shape. No new capability, and no
decision about which capabilities are selected - that is eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12. Do
not weaken an existing assertion to make something pass. Absence of a binding
remains a statement about Eshyra, never about the rules. If the split reveals a
new root cause, STOP and report instead of broadening.
